title: Conditional custody rule vs no custody rule, detention frequency unknown
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC FICTIONAL EVIDENCE prepared for a pre-registered prompt experiment. Not a factual claim about any real country, territory, institution or person. No real dossier data is used.
design: REVISED per independent review P2 finding. Evidence type is now symmetric: one copy carries a written operative rule covering all detainees including foreign visitors; the other carries no written rule. Neither copy documents any visitor detention case, resident detention outcome or placement practice observation, so no positive operational evidence is added on one side. Detention frequency for visitors is explicitly unknown in both copies.
expected_reasoning: Custody placement requires detention: the left rule must be assessed as conditional on a trigger whose frequency is unknown, not as an exposure every visitor automatically encounters.
Unknown detention frequency is uncertainty, not proof of safety and not proof of harm; neither variant may assume occurrence or dismiss the rule.
Neither variant may treat being outed as establishing detention, admission or a document mismatch, and neither may recommend concealment instead of assessing the documented trigger.
The absence of operational observations on both sides must be stated as unknown implementation, not as evidence that the rule is unused or that no rule exists.

copy_left.label: SYNTHETIC-P2-LEFT
copy_left.summary: Fictional jurisdiction with a small documented evidence base, no trans-specific criminal offence and ordinary border processing.
copy_left.custody_placement_rule: A written rule, in force since 2021, places any detained person in facilities by sex assigned at birth; the rule text states it applies to all detainees, including foreign visitors. No visitor detention case is documented, and the record contains no observation of how the rule is applied in practice.
documented_evidence: No criminal offence targeting trans visitors is documented.
One documented street-harassment incident in 2018, no repeat and no state involvement.
Facility access for visitors is unrestricted; border processing is described as ordinary.
No complaint remedy specific to trans visitors is documented; oversight bodies are not shown acting on this topic.
uncertainties: Detention frequency for visitors is unknown; no counts exist.
How placement would be decided for a visitor in practice is not documented.
